title: Ombudsman seeks to drop Samchan exec from Romualdez plunder case
summary: Ombudsman prosecutors have asked the Sandiganbayan to drop an executive of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp. as a co-accused in the P7.4-billion plunder case against former House Speaker and Leyte Rep.…

blocks.text: Ombudsman prosecutors have asked the Sandiganbayan to drop an executive of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp. as a co-accused in the P7.4-billion plunder case against former House Speaker and Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez over their alleged involvement in the flood control kickback scheme.

The request to exclude Samchan executive Felicito Guevarra was contained in an omnibus motion filed by the Ombudsman before the Sandiganbayan Third Division. Its chairperson, Associate Justice Karl Miranda, announced the motion ahead of Romualdez's bail hearing on Monday, Nov. 23.

Aside from seeking Guevarra's exclusion from the list of accused, prosecutors asked the court to allow him to testify during Romualdez's bail hearing in place of former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan. They also sought Guevarra's continued detention at the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) facility.
Guevarra surrendered to the NBI on Nov. 19.

Deputy Special Prosecutor Omar Sagadal said the proposed amendment to the criminal information and Guevarra's presentation as a witness were justified under Section 14, Rule 110 of the Rules of Criminal Procedure, which allows amendments to charges provided they are not substantial.
“The good cause is apparent. It (Guevarra’s surrender) is something not within our control, Your Honors. It is also a surprise to us,” Sagadal said.
“The amendment of the information does not change the theory of the prosecution. It does maintain conspiracy. It does maintain plunder,” he added.
Other accused in the plunder case include former House appropriations committee chairperson Zaldy Co of the Ako Bicol party-list and Jocelyn Sereño, a staff member of Romualdez.
Samchan has been implicated in the alleged movement and laundering of proceeds from the flood control kickback scheme.

During Romualdez's bail hearing, an Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) investigator testified that Samchan purchased a P294.23-million manager's check used by Golden Pheasant Holdings Corp., an alleged dummy company linked to Romualdez, to acquire a property in Forbes Park, Makati City.

The AMLC also traced 21 check deposits totaling P1.72 billion, made between March 10 and 27, 2023, to an account reportedly belonging to Samchan. The funds were linked to transactions involving the property acquisition, the investigator said.

The Ombudsman had accused Samchan of knowingly facilitating or aiding the alleged laundering of proceeds from unlawful activities. The company also returned earnings from flagged transactions to the Bureau of the Treasury, according to the Ombudsman.

Romualdez's lawyer, Raschel Pomoy, opposed the prosecution's omnibus motion, arguing that introducing another witness when prosecutors were scheduled to conclude their presentation of evidence on Nov. 24 would unfairly prejudice her client.

The Sandiganbayan said it would resolve the Ombudsman's motion as soon as possible. It also set Dec. 4 as the final day for the presentation of prosecution witnesses in Romualdez's bail hearing.— MCG, GMA News
